To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) unrelated donor bone marrow transplant (BMT) recipients who received low-dose ATG had equivalent survival and disease-free survival to matched sibling BMIT recipients, (2) unrelated donor BMT recipients with low/intermmediate risk leukemia had superior disease-free survival to those with high-risk leukemia, and (3) the use of unrelated donor BMT should now be considered in any situation where matched sibling BMT is routine.
unrelated donor (UD BMT recipients) given pretransplant antithymocyte globalin (ATG) have outcomes equivalent to recipients of genotypicall matched related donor (RD) BMT.
the use of thymoglobulin pretransplant in UD BMT is associated with a significant reduction in the incidence of grade III–IV GVHD and a significant improvement in overall survival.

the results of unrelated BMT are equivalent to matched related transplants.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of ATG in UD BMT is a viable alternative to T cell depletion, and it may be a better choice because of lower cost and the ability to use the grafts that are not suitable for T cell depletion.
the outcomes of unrelated donor BMT can be as good as matched sibling BMT, and in fact, the outcomes for high risk patients are better with the use of ATG.
